metadata.description: A powerful taxi 'mother' organization in Cape Town, notorious for its involvement in violent turf wars and competition for lucrative routes.
A major taxi association in Cape Town and the primary rival of CATA. Involved in long-standing violent conflicts over taxi territory.
The national representative body for the minibus taxi industry in South Africa, often mediating between the government and local associations.

notable_actions: Declared a violent taxi strike in August 2023

metadata.description: Ongoing turf wars between taxi associations and individual operators since the late 1980s, driven by deregulation and competition for passengers.

key_attributes.death_toll: Thousands (historically 200-300 deaths annually in the late 90s)

metadata.description: A series of organized arson attacks on Metrorail passenger trains in Cape Town, frequently linked to the taxi industry aiming to reduce rail competition.
A mass shooting on 2 November 2020 in Gugulethu that left eight people dead, linked to local gang conflicts and extortion.

suspected_motives: Conflict between Guptas and Boko Haram gangs

metadata.description: Two mass shootings at homesteads in Lusikisiki on 28 September 2024, resulting in 18 fatalities.

key_attributes.context: One of the deadliest mass shootings in recent South African history.

metadata.description: A local street gang in Gugulethu, Cape Town, known for extorting residents and businesses.
A street gang in Gugulethu involved in territorial conflicts with the Boko Haram gang.
Former policeman and security guard known as 'The Apartheid Killer'. Convicted of 7 murders but suspected of up to 39, mostly targeting black people.
Former police sergeant at Tembisa station convicted of murdering six relatives for insurance payouts.
Serial killer and rapist known as 'The Century City Killer', who targeted young jobseekers near Cape Town train stations.
A significant case where thirteen police officers were charged with complicity in taxi violence, illustrating the depth of corruption in the industry's regulation.

key_attributes.implication: State/Police involvement in destabilizing political opposition through taxi turf wars.

metadata.description: A massacre resulting from a taxi dispute between competing operators on Christmas Day 2020.
White supremacist known for the Strijdom Square massacre. Claimed he wanted to start a race war.
A black taxi driver who heroically stopped white supremacist Barend Strydom during his shooting spree in 1988.

key_attributes.action: Disarmed Strydom at Sato Engineering building

edges.description: Primary rivals in the Cape Town taxi industry, frequently engaging in violent turf wars.
CATA is a major participant in the ongoing taxi wars.
CODETA is a central organization involved in the taxi wars.
Santaco represents the industry and has been involved in major strikes and conflicts.
Taxi operators (including members of CATA/CODETA) are suspected of orchestrating train arson to force commuters onto taxis.
Taxi operators are linked to arson attacks on rail services to eliminate competition.
Mass shooting suspected to be an act of extortion or territorial warfare by the Boko Haram gang.
Official charges against 13 police officers confirmed state/police complicity in taxi violence.
A recent high-casualty event in the ongoing taxi wars.
Mukondoleli disarmed and stopped Strydom's shooting spree.
While unrelated to the 1998 case, Ndlovu represents a modern example of severe police criminality.
Van Schoor represents the legacy of apartheid-era police complicity in violence against black South Africans.
